title: Discover, Design, Acquire and Build

header.html: The ITIL Product and Service Lifecycle (10%)
Know the purpose of discover, design, acquire and build; define product specification, product prototype, test, continuous integration; understand the key success metrics of the activities
the official ITIL Foundation (Version 5) syllabus, version 5.0 (February 2026), categories 3.2.1 to 3.2.4, 4.4.2, 4.4.4, 4.4.5 and 4.4.11

html:
1Discover

Purpose: keep the product and service roadmap aligned with what consumers need and with the organization's strategy. [Verify live]

What happens Example
Understand consumers and the market interviews, feedback, demand analysis
Spot opportunities and threats a competitor launches a new feature
Decide what to pursue update the roadmap

Typical success metrics: consumer satisfaction with ideas, share of roadmap items with a clear value case. [Verify live]

2Design

Purpose: turn validated needs into a product specification, architecture and prototypes that can be built.

Term Meaning
Product specification A written description of what the product must be and do (features, quality, limits)
Product prototype An early, working or visual model used to test ideas with users before full build
Exam tip

. Specification = the description. Prototype = the early model to test. Both are produced in design.

Typical success metrics: stakeholder approval of designs, share of designs validated with users. [Verify live]

3Acquire

Purpose: secure and allocate the resources needed to build the product: people, tools, hardware, software, services, licenses.

Acquire covers buying, hiring, renting or licensing, and managing the suppliers involved. Typical success metrics: resources available when needed, cost against budget. [Verify live]

4Build

Purpose: create, configure and test the technology and components that make up the product or service.

Term Meaning
Test Checking that a component or product meets its requirements and works correctly
Continuous integration (CI) Frequently merging code changes into a shared place with automatic build and test

Typical success metrics: defects found before release, build and test cycle time. [Verify live]

Exam tip

. CI = merge often and test automatically. (Continuous delivery and deployment are in Module 7.)

Exam tip

. Match the verb to the activity: find out is discover, specify and prototype is design, get resources is acquire, create and test is build.

5Exam Q&A

5.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1Which activity keeps the roadmap aligned with consumer needs and organizational strategy?

  • ABuild
  • BDiscover
  • CTransition
  • DSupport
Show the answer

Answer: B. That is the purpose of discover.

S2A team produces an early clickable model and tests it with five users. Which term applies?

  • ARelease
  • BService level agreement
  • CProduct prototype
  • DKnown error
Show the answer

Answer: C. A prototype is an early model used to test ideas.

S3Which statement about the build activity is CORRECT? (1) It creates, configures and tests the product. (2) It includes testing against requirements. (3) It decides the strategic direction of the organization. (4) It restores service after an incident.

  • A1 and 2
  • B3 and 4
  • C2 and 3
  • D1 and 4
Show the answer

Answer: A. Build creates, configures and tests.

S4Identify the missing word(s). [ ? ] is the practice of frequently merging code changes with automatic build and test.

  • AContinuous integration
  • BContinuous deployment
  • CObservability
  • DKnown error management
Show the answer

Answer: A. Continuous integration merges often and tests automatically.

S5A product manager secures developers, cloud licenses and a testing tool for a new product. Which activity is this?

  • AAcquire
  • BDiscover
  • CDesign
  • DDeliver
Show the answer

Answer: A. Acquire secures and allocates resources.

S6Which output belongs to the design activity?

  • AAn incident record
  • BA service request
  • CA disaster plan
  • DA product specification
Show the answer

Answer: D. Design produces specifications, architectures and prototypes.

5.2 Recall questions

R1What is the purpose of discover?

Show the answer

To keep the roadmap aligned with consumer needs and strategy.

R2What is a product specification?

Show the answer

A written description of what the product must be and do.

R3What is a product prototype?

Show the answer

An early model used to test ideas before the full build.

R4What does acquire do?

Show the answer

Secures and allocates the resources needed to build.

R5What does build do?

Show the answer

Creates, configures and tests the product.

R6What is continuous integration?

Show the answer

Frequently merging code with automatic build and test.

6Quick Reference Card

Activity Purpose Key terms
Discover align roadmap with needs and strategy consumer needs
Design needs into specification and prototypes product specification, prototype
Acquire secure resources people, tools, suppliers
Build create, configure, test test, continuous integration
